findings.description: diffHunks pins inter-hunk context but not the diff algorithm: a session-written `diff.algorithm=patience` (or `histogram`) in the shared config makes the -U0 patch report unchanged, test-covered lines as added, diluting patch coverage the same way decision 113's interHunkContext attack does.
findings.body:
**Concern.** Decision 113 pins `--inter-hunk-context=0` because a session-written `diff.interHunkContext` makes `diffHunks` report unchanged lines as added. `patchCoverage` (`src/core/coverage.utils.ts#L36-L54`) then counts them, and since tests already cover them, an untested change gets lifted over the bar. `diff.algorithm` is a second key that does the same thing. It sits in the same shared `$GIT_COMMON_DIR/config` (decision 50), porcelain `git diff` reads it, and `DIFF_SAFE_FLAGS` (`--no-ext-diff --no-textconv --no-color --text`) does not override it. `GIT_SAFE_CONFIG` does not either.

Patience and histogram anchor only on lines that appear once in each file, so their output can be far from minimal. An example:

- Base file: `U1`, then 100 repeated covered statements, then `U2`.
- Branch file: `U2`, the same 100 statements, then `U1`.
- Under myers (the default), the -U0 patch shows 2 added lines.
- Under `diff.algorithm=patience`, patience can anchor on only one of `U1`/`U2`. The 100 unchanged lines then come out as deleted and re-added, so `gitDiffAddedLines` lists about 101 added lines, all of them instrumented and covered.

Untested new code elsewhere in the branch is diluted below the bar's denominator. No diff shows the config change, and a reviewer reading a default (myers) diff sees only a 2-line swap. The session writes the file content, so it can build this shape. The inflation also appears in `--numstat`, but that only feeds the oversize *flag*, while patch coverage *blocks*.

The fix belongs with the inter-hunk pin: a command-line `--diff-algorithm` overrides the config key. `gitDiffNumstat` does not need it, because a non-minimal algorithm only inflates the size count, which works against the attacker.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/b4f9f54c9dc2094ae6f979efe3482b73b3ac1574/src/core/git-diff.client.ts#L512-L521

findings.description: `--literal-pathspecs` makes git die ("global 'literal' pathspec setting is incompatible...") when the operator's env has GIT_GLOB_PATHSPECS/GIT_NOGLOB_PATHSPECS/GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS set, and scrubbedGitEnv does not strip them; it fails loud, but adding the three names to scrubbedGitEnv's list would avoid the throw.

Decision 53 still says `core.bigFileThreshold=1` forges a null numstat, but decision 113 now pins it to 512m; add an `*Amended by decision 113:*` note, as the doc does for other amended decisions (e.g. lines 328, 373, 563).

Decision 113's threshold paragraph says `--text` restores the patch so decision 53's recount finds the lines, then says the patch lost its hunks too, leaving gitDiffAddedLines at 0; the two claims contradict each other. State which one was reproduced.
"Both pins are on their own call rather than in DIFF_SAFE_FLAGS or GIT_SAFE_CONFIG" is ambiguous in a paragraph that introduces only the rename pin; name them ("the rename and inter-hunk pins").

The gitDiffNumstat comment "score a new file copied from a changed one as that copy's edits alone" is vague; the decision's wording (scored as a diff against the source's old content, so the copy counts only its edits) is clearer.

The `-c diff.renames=true` pin is inline in gitDiffNumstat only, while gitDiffPaths' `--name-only` diff is still exposed to a session-written diff.renames; the rule for which pins go in GIT_SAFE_CONFIG, DIFF_SAFE_FLAGS, or per call is left implicit.
